requirements.requirement: Show “Position uncertain” after three seconds of continuous uncertainty.
Hide lane-level guidance immediately when positioning becomes unreliable.
While waiting for GPS, retain the last location view, allow panning and provide recentering without forced snap-backs.
Use available phone sensors, including the gyroscope, to support positioning and direction.
Keep the route line on your carriageway, leaving the opposite carriageway visible where possible.
Place the vehicle marker near the bottom of the map so more road ahead is visible.
Colour affected route sections amber for slower traffic and red for heavy congestion.
Keep the vehicle arrow centred on your carriageway, following the road direction and proportional to the map.
Adjust the driving camera using location, road type, actual speed and distance to the next turn.
Far from a junction, tilt toward the horizon and zoom out to show more of the path ahead.
Near a junction, zoom in gradually and tilt toward an overhead view, keeping the vehicle and turn visible.
Keep camera and zoom movement smooth, without sudden jumps.
Include the following turn in the visible map when two turns are close together.
Highlight all suitable lanes, favouring those needed for a closely following turn.
Provide detailed lane diagrams to make driving easier.
Initially show detailed lane diagrams at complex junctions.
Prepare lane guidance early enough to allow time to get into position.
Vary lane-guidance timing with speed: earlier on motorways and later in town.
Provide 3D immersive driving guidance.
Show a faster route using an avoided road as a clearly warned alternative, and use it only when explicitly selected.
Allow the route-results panel to be dragged down to reveal more of the map and the routes beneath it.
Reroute automatically and straight away when the driver goes off-route.
